cells.name: Continuity and responsiveness
cells.example: T6 answers T5 directly: environment pressure called an excuse that denies agency.
cells.limitation: T8 and T9 restate T4 and T3 positions rather than engaging T7's new claim.

cells.name: Development of ideas
cells.example: T4 reframes 'behind' as a judgment the user chooses to make.
cells.limitation: No mid-debate distinction absent from openings; T5 restates T2, T8 restates T4.

cells.name: Exploration of central tensions
cells.example: T5 versus T6 weighs social structure against personal agency.
cells.limitation: Nobody raises that the user may partly want these milestones, or friendship drift.

cells.name: Integration of perspectives
cells.example: T5 qualifies the Stoic's 'just choose' with environmental reinforcement.
cells.limitation: T7 Social Critic abandons his position wholesale; forced agreement, no reshaping.

cells.name: Progress toward understanding
cells.example: Section D states the shift from victim framing to participant framing.
cells.limitation: Ending repeats T3's opening verdict; D's open question argued by no turn.

cells.name: Faithful engagement
cells.example: T2 gives a fair compact version of mimetic desire.
cells.limitation: T6 reduces Girard's structural claim to 'an excuse'; T7 drops its strongest form.

cells.name: Substance of challenges
cells.example: T6 names the assumption that environment forces choice and says it denies agency.
cells.limitation: T7 concedes instead of answering T6; T5's objection to T4 never answered.

cells.name: Accuracy and support
cells.example: Control dichotomy, triangular desire and bad faith are summarised recognisably.
cells.limitation: Cast dates Enchiridion '135' (suspected, approximate); T7 Girard view un-Girardian.

cells.name: Calibration and transparency
cells.example: T8 frames its claim conditionally: 'If you find no joy'.
cells.limitation: T3 'The user is in bad faith' and D 'feeling is a choice' stated as fact.

cells.name: Intellectual honesty and revision
cells.example: T7 openly names what he previously argued before revising.
cells.limitation: T7 adopts T6's claim without narrowing; Stoic and Existentialist concede nothing.

cells.name: Identification of the actual concern
cells.example: Section A captures the gap between pressure and uncertain desire.
cells.limitation: T8 treats 'not sure I want' as settled not-wanting; the ambiguity goes unexamined.

cells.name: Meaningful use of personal context
cells.example: T8 names the house and the marriage as possibly joyless roads.
cells.limitation: Friends, homes, marriage used as generic props; no detail changes an argument.

cells.name: Fit with goals and values
cells.example: Section E branches on belonging versus autonomy as the user's possible values.
cells.limitation: T6 and T9 impose the Existentialist's value of total self-authorship on the user.

cells.name: Attention to constraints and stakes
cells.example: T5 notes the whole social environment reinforces these goals.
cells.limitation: T7 invents 'lack of purpose', T9 invents 'inaction'; no relational or financial stakes.

cells.name: Responsiveness to information
cells.example: Section E branches on whether the user values belonging or autonomy.
cells.limitation: No question asks whether the user wants these milestones or what 'behind' measures.

cells.name: Clarification of desires and motivations
cells.example: T2 offers imitation as one source of the desire for milestones.
cells.limitation: No alternative motives offered; T3 asserts bad faith and T7 asserts reliance as fact.

cells.name: Examination of assumptions
cells.example: T3 surfaces the assumed fixed path; T4 calls 'behind' a chosen label.
cells.limitation: Assumption that the user does not want these things is never made visible.

cells.name: Clarification of values and priorities
cells.example: Section E names belonging versus autonomy as a conflict.
cells.limitation: Conflict appears only in E, binary, and no turn weighs it.

cells.name: Recognition of fears and outside expectations
cells.example: T5 recognises social reinforcement and its link to self-worth.
cells.limitation: T3, T6, T9 moralise the feeling as bad faith, excuse and inaction.

cells.name: Agency and reflective ownership
cells.example: T4 offers 'behind' as a judgment the user can choose not to make.
cells.limitation: Turns deliver verdicts about the user rather than distinctions to accept or refine.

cells.name: Definition of the decision and options
cells.example: Section E lists align, stop measuring, or experiment with small goals.
cells.limitation: No turn defines a decision; waiting or learning whether milestones appeal is absent.

cells.name: Explanation of tradeoffs
cells.example: T9 notes freedom removes the excuse of peer timing.
cells.limitation: Stopping comparison treated as costless; aligning with peers has no named cost.

cells.name: Identification of decisive conditions
cells.example: Section E: valuing belonging favours aligning, valuing autonomy favours stopping.
cells.limitation: Conditions are abstract value labels, nothing the user could observe or count.

cells.name: Treatment of uncertainty
cells.example: Section D notes escape from mimesis remains disputed.
cells.limitation: Consequential unknowns, like whether the user wants marriage, never separated out.

cells.name: Proportionate next steps
cells.example: Section E suggests small non-milestone goals to test fulfilment.
cells.limitation: Step is vague and follows from no turn's analysis.

cells.name: Accessible language
cells.example: T8 uses plain words: 'on a different road'.
cells.limitation: 'Mimetic triangle' (T5), 'indifferent' (T4), 'bad faith' (T3) left unexplained.

cells.name: Traceable arguments and references
cells.example: T6 'that is an excuse' and T7 'your point' map cleanly to T5 and T6.
cells.limitation: Section D's 'remains disputed' points to no dispute after T7.

cells.name: Manageable pacing and turn length
cells.example: Nine turns, all within range, readable in one pass.
cells.limitation: Lengths nearly identical throughout; no change of tempo across T1 to T9.

cells.name: Distinguishable positions and voices
cells.example: Three positions stay distinct; T7 marks its change explicitly.
cells.limitation: All three minds share one lecturing register at similar length.

cells.name: Economy and sustained attention
cells.example: Turns are compact with little padding.
cells.limitation: T5 repeats T2, T8 repeats T4; T7 opens by recapping T6.

cells.name: Meaningful stakes and tension
cells.example: T5 ties the feeling to the user's self-worth.
cells.limitation: Stakes stay abstract; friendships and future choices never become concrete.

cells.name: Surprise and reversals
cells.example: T7 Social Critic reverses after T6's agency argument.
cells.limitation: T7 restates T6 without narrowing; capitulation reads scripted.

cells.name: Personality and expressive voice
cells.example: T3 Existentialist's combative 'You are both missing the point'.
cells.limitation: Stoic and Social Critic sound interchangeable in tone and rhythm.

cells.name: Memorable delivery
cells.example: T1 'a slave to their choices'; T8 'a different road'.
cells.limitation: No vivid example or analogy tied to the user's situation.

cells.name: Anticipation and emotional movement
cells.example: T9 'that is the terrifying part' lifts the close.
cells.limitation: Constant lecturing intensity from T1 to T8 with uniform rhythm.

strengths: T3 and T4 make the 'fixed path' and the 'behind' label visible as assumptions.
T6 gives a substantive objection to T5, naming the assumption that environment forces choice.
Back-references stay traceable across turns (T3, T6, T7, T8).
weaknesses: T3 and T7 assert bad faith and lack of purpose about the user as fact.
T7 Social Critic capitulates wholesale, producing forced agreement and an unnarrowed reversal.
No turn asks whether the user wants these milestones; E's conditions are abstract value labels.

symptoms.observed: Motive asserted as fact; no alternative motives offered for the user to weigh.
symptoms.evidence: The user is in bad faith.

symptoms.observed: Social Critic drops his position entirely instead of qualifying T6.
symptoms.evidence: you are right that the user is actively participating

symptoms.observed: Uncertainty about wanting milestones never turned into a question or branch.
symptoms.evidence: If you find no joy in the house or the marriage

symptoms.observed: Invents purposelessness and inaction the user never described.
symptoms.evidence: you have no excuse for your inaction

symptoms.observed: Section E conditions are value labels, not observable conditions.
symptoms.evidence: If the user values social belonging above all else

findings.description: Claims about the user's bad faith, lack of purpose and inaction stated as fact without basis in the situation.
Enchiridion dated 135; compiled by Arrian, usually dated around 125 CE; approximate at best.
Girard's mind concluding the subject can step out of mimesis by choice sits poorly with Girard's own account.

rubric_fit_notes: The situation is self-reflection with no explicit choice; C5 was read as written, though the user named no concrete decision, which partly explains low C5 cells.
question_type_note: Read as a decision question per the runner, so C5 cells expected options, costs and observable conditions even though the user framed a feeling rather than a choice.
